_readme: Byte-exact goldens for moxie_sdk/automarkup.py, from docs/architecture/backlog/expressiveness.md §1.6. Regenerate ONLY when the floor's rules change on purpose, and read the diff: every byte here is something a child sees the robot do. Two documented departures from the brief's hand-written shorthand: (a) G4 keeps the space between two sentences, because invariant S2 says the spoken words never change and `strip_markup` would otherwise fuse "amazing!You"; (b) G8 places Gesture_Point before the line rather than after, consistent with G1 and G6, which both pin a leading gesture mark.

cases.why: `!` -> Happy (mood 1) + `excited` genre; `I` is a self word -> Gesture_Self; the internal sentence boundary earns a break; the line ends at rest.

cases.text: What do you want to play today?
cases.why: `?` -> `question` genre; an open question is Curious (mood 9); `what` is a question word -> Gesture_Question. No break: it is the final word, and a break there would delay the robot's turn hand-back.

cases.text: Hmm, let me think about that.
cases.why: leading interjection comma -> break; thinking cue -> Curious + Bht_Active_Thinking (an app-hardcoded tree the SIM renders). A sentence that plays a whole-body tree gets no arm gesture stacked on it.

cases.text: That is amazing! You did it!
cases.why: two `!` -> intensity 2 (clamped at maxIntensity); `amazing` is a high word -> Gesture_Higher; the praise phrase `you did it` -> Gesture_Celebrate. Gestures for a `<usel>`-wrapped sentence are minted after the span, never inside it.

cases.text: Oh! I did not know that.
cases.why: mood 5 Surprised is the value shipped content uses for exactly this - "Oh!", 14 occurrences (behavior-markup.md:122) - and it beats the generic `!` -> Happy rule.

cases.why: mood 2 Sad is what shipped content uses for "I'm sorry...", 8 occurrences (behavior-markup.md:119); no `!`/`?` so no `<usel>`.

mood 4 Shy is shipped content's value for "Oops.", 2 occurrences (behavior-markup.md:121) - and note the earlier *inferred* reading mislabeled 4 as "embarrassed". One word is far under the talking-gesture floor, so it gets no arm gesture at all: the anti-twitch rule in action.

`Birthday` is one of the four confirmed icon values; a turn shows command:0 before the line and clears with command:2 after; `your` points at the child (Gesture_Point - our catalog has no "you" gesture, so we do NOT borrow OpenMoxie's AUTO_GESTURE_YOU).
